candidate.answerReason: The first three sons receive 19/20 of the herd, leaving 1/20 equal to 7 cows. Thus the herd contains 140 cows.

methods.label: Find the remaining fraction
methods.explanation:
All three stated fractions refer to the whole herd. Together, the first three sons receive
\[
\frac12+\frac14+\frac15
=\frac{10+5+4}{20}
=\frac{19}{20}.
\]
The fourth son therefore receives \(1-\frac{19}{20}=\frac1{20}\) of the herd. Since that share is \(7\) cows, the whole herd has
\[
n=7\div\frac1{20}=7\cdot20=140
\]
cows. The resulting shares are \(70,35,28,7\), all whole numbers totaling \(140\). The answer is \(140\), choice C.
methods.levelReason: Adding fractional shares and recovering the whole from a known fractional part gives an elementary arithmetic solution.
